name: text/template used to render HTML (no auto-escaping)
attack_scenario: A handler builds its HTML page with text/template; a username of is interpolated unescaped and executes as script in the victim's browser.
negative_test_hint: render the page with username "" and assert the output HTML-escapes the value as inert text instead of executing it

exemplar.noncompliant: import "text/template"   // then t.Execute(w, userData) into an HTML response
exemplar.compliant: import "html/template"   // context-aware auto-escaping for HTML output
exemplar.explanation: text/template performs zero contextual escaping; only html/template does. Using text/template to build any HTML that reaches a browser means every interpolated value is a raw injection point. text/template is legitimate for config files, plain-text emails, and code generation, so this is a medium review flag: confirm the output is never served as HTML, otherwise switch the import to html/template.
